form.label: Data Model & Pivot
form.description: Analyze the lab's data with no SPL — point-and-click, via the DCloudLab data model.

html.h2: Data models & Pivot — analytics without writing SPL
html.p: New to Splunk? A data model is a friendly, named map over your raw data (fields grouped into datasets like Host Metrics, Web Requests, Network). Pivot then lets you build tables and charts by clicking — pick a dataset, choose "split by" and a measure — no search language needed. We shipped a model called dCloudLab covering the whole lab.
RBAC still applies: the model spans all locations, but Pivot only shows you data your role can read (Leo → London, Ben → Berlin, Gary → all).

ol.li: Top menu: Settings → Data models → dCloud Lab, then click Pivot on a dataset (Lab Events, Host Metrics, Web Requests, Network).
Or from the Datasets page → find a dCloudLab dataset → Explore ▸ Visualize with Pivot.

panel.title: Example (via the model) — events by asset type & site

search.query: | datamodel DCloudLab LabEvents search | stats count as Events by asset_type, site | rename asset_type as "Asset type", site as Site | sort - Events

panel.title: Example (via the model) — CPU % over time by site

search.query: | datamodel DCloudLab HostMetrics search | timechart span=5m avg(cpu_pct) as "CPU %" by site

ul.li: Lab Events (root) — everything, with Host, Sourcetype, Index, Site, and the asset fields (Asset name / type / Manufacturer).
Host Metrics — CPU %, Memory %, Disk %, Load (numbers you can average).
Web Requests — Method, Path, Status, Source IP (from the web-app container).
Network (Cisco show) — Command (from the router SSH polling).

html.p: Under the hood these panels use | datamodel DCloudLab <dataset> search … — but in Pivot you never type that; you click. Try: open Host Metrics in Pivot, split by Site, and add Average of CPU % as a column chart.
